sanskrit: tāṃ māṃ svayam anuprāptām abhinanda śacīpate tvayārcitāṃ māṃ deveśa purodhāsyanti devatāḥ
english: Welcome me, lord of Śacī, for I have come to you of my own accord; honored by you, O lord of the gods, the deities will set me at their head.

sanskrit: yatrāhaṃ tatra matkāntā madviśiṣṭā madarpaṇāḥ sapta devyo mayāṣṭamyo vāsaṃ ceṣyanti me 'ṣṭadhā
english: Wherever I am, there too will dwell my beloved companions—those who cleave to me and offer themselves to me: seven goddesses, with myself the eighth, will abide eightfold at my side.

sanskrit: āśā śraddhā dhṛtiḥ kāntir vijitiḥ sannatiḥ kṣamā aṣṭamī vṛttir etāsāṃ purogā pākaśāsana
english: Hope, Faith, Constancy, Beauty, Victory, Humility, Forbearance—and Conduct as the eighth, who walks before them all, O chastiser of Pāka.

sanskrit: tāś cāhaṃ cāsurāṃs tyaktvā yuṣmadviṣayam āgatā tridaśeṣu nivatsyāmo dharmaniṣṭhāntarātmasu
english: They and I, forsaking the Asuras, have come into your domain; among the Thirty Gods we shall dwell, whose inmost selves are fixed in dharma.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktavacanāṃ devīm atyarthaṃ tau nanandatuḥ nāradaś ca trilokarṣir vṛtrahantā ca vāsavaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: When the goddess had spoken these words, the two rejoiced exceedingly—Nārada, the sage of the three worlds, and Vāsava, the slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tato 'nalasakho vāyuḥ pravavau devaveśmasu iṣṭagandhaḥ sukhasparśaḥ sarvendriyasukhāvahaḥ
english: Then through the dwellings of the gods blew the Wind, the friend of Fire, fragrant and welcome, soft to the touch, bringing delight to every sense.

sanskrit: śucau cābhyarcite deśe tridaśāḥ prāyaśaḥ sthitāḥ lakṣmyā sahitam āsīnaṃ maghavantaṃ didṛkṣavaḥ
english: In a place pure and adorned the Thirty Gods stood for the most part assembled, eager to behold Maghavat seated together with Lakṣmī.

sanskrit: tato divaṃ prāpya sahasralocanaḥ; śriyopapannaḥ suhṛdā surarṣiṇā rathena haryaśvayujā surarṣabhaḥ; sadaḥ surāṇām abhisatkṛto yayau
english: Then the Thousand-eyed One, reaching heaven endowed with Śrī, with his friend the divine sage beside him, that bull among gods, drove in his chariot yoked with bay steeds, and went, well honored, to the assembly hall of the gods.

sanskrit: atheṅgitaṃ vajradharasya nāradaḥ; śriyāś ca devyā manasā vicārayan śriyai śaśaṃsāmaradṛṣṭapauruṣaḥ; śivena tatrāgamanaṃ maharddhimat
english: Then Nārada, pondering in his mind the bearing of the wielder of the thunderbolt and of the goddess Śrī—he whose manhood the gods had witnessed—announced to Śrī that her coming there, in auspicious fashion, would be one of great prosperity.

sanskrit: tato 'mṛtaṃ dyauḥ pravavarṣa bhāsvatī; pitāmahasyāyatane svayaṃbhuvaḥ anāhatā dundubhayaś ca nedire; tathā prasannāś ca diśaś cakāśire
english: Then the radiant sky rained down nectar over the abode of the Self-existent Grandsire; drums sounded untouched by any hand, and the quarters of the world, grown serene, shone bright.

sanskrit: yathartu sasyeṣu vavarṣa vāsavo; na dharmamārgād vicacāla kaś cana anekaratnākarabhūṣaṇā ca bhūḥ; sughoṣaghoṣā bhuvanaukasāṃ jaye
english: Vāsava rained upon the crops each in its season, and not a soul strayed from the path of dharma; the earth, adorned with mines of many jewels, rang with auspicious sound at the triumph of the world's dwellers.

sanskrit: kriyābhirāmā manujā yaśasvino; babhuḥ śubhe puṇyakṛtāṃ pathi sthitāḥ narāmarāḥ kiṃnarayakṣarākṣasāḥ; samṛddhimantaḥ sukhino yaśasvinaḥ
english: Men delighting in sacred rites grew glorious, standing firm on the blessed road of the doers of good; humans and gods, Kiṃnaras, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas became prosperous, happy, and renowned.

sanskrit: na jātv akāle kusumaṃ kutaḥ phalaṃ; papāta vṛkṣāt pavaneritād api rasapradāḥ kāmadughāś ca dhenavo; na dāruṇā vāg vicacāra kasya cit
english: Never did a blossom—much less a fruit—fall untimely from a tree, even when shaken by the wind; the cows yielded sweet milk and granted every wish, and no harsh word passed from anyone's lips.

sanskrit: imāṃ saparyāṃ saha sarvakāmadaiḥ; śriyāś ca śakrapramukhaiś ca daivataiḥ paṭhanti ye viprasadaḥ samāgame; samṛddhakāmāḥ śriyam āpnuvanti te
english: Those brāhmaṇas who in their assemblies recite this worship of Śrī, together with the deities led by Śakra who grant all desires, attain Śrī, their every wish fulfilled.

sanskrit: tvayā kurūṇāṃ vara yat pracoditaṃ; bhavābhavasyeha paraṃ nidarśanam tad adya sarvaṃ parikīrtitaṃ mayā; parīkṣya tattvaṃ parigantum arhasi
english: What you, O best of the Kurus, urged me to tell—the supreme illustration here of prosperity and ruin—all that I have now recounted in full; weighing its truth, you ought to grasp it whole.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃśīlaḥ kiṃsamācāraḥ kiṃvidyaḥ kiṃparāyaṇaḥ prāpnoti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ yat paraṃ prakṛter dhruvam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of what character, what conduct, what learning, what refuge is the man who attains the abode of Brahman, that which is supreme, beyond Nature, and unchanging?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mokṣadharmeṣu niyato laghvāhāro jitendriyaḥ prāpnoti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ yat paraṃ prakṛter dhruvam
english: Bhīṣma said: He who is steadfast in the disciplines of liberation, sparing in food, and master of his senses attains the abode of Brahman, that which is supreme, beyond Nature, and unchanging.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam jaigīṣavyasya saṃvādam asitasya ca bhārata
english: On this point too they relate an ancient tale, O descendant of Bharata: the dialogue of Jaigīṣavya and Asita.

sanskrit: jaigīṣavyaṃ mahāprājñaṃ dharmāṇām āgatāgamam akrudhyantam ahṛṣyantam asito devalo 'bravīt
english: To Jaigīṣavya, the greatly wise, versed in the whole tradition of the dharmas, who neither grew angry nor elated, Asita Devala spoke.

sanskrit: na prīyase vandyamāno nindyamāno na kupyasi kā te prajñā kutaś caiṣā kiṃ caitasyāḥ parāyaṇam
english: When praised, you take no pleasure; when blamed, you feel no anger. What is this wisdom of yours, whence does it come, and what is its final ground?

sanskrit: iti tenānuyuktaḥ sa tam uvāca mahātapāḥ mahad vākyam asaṃdigdhaṃ puṣkalārthapadaṃ śuci
english: Thus questioned by him, that great ascetic spoke to him a lofty utterance, free of doubt, rich in meaning and words, and pure.

sanskrit: yā gatir yā parā niṣṭhā yā śāntiḥ puṇyakarmaṇām tāṃ te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yan māṃ pṛcchasi vai dvija
english: That course, that highest consummation, that peace which belongs to the doers of meritorious deeds—of this I shall tell you fully, O brāhmaṇa, since you ask it of me.

sanskrit: nindatsu ca samo nityaṃ praśaṃsatsu ca devala nihnuvanti ca ye teṣāṃ samayaṃ sukṛtaṃ ca ye
english: Ever even-minded toward those who blame and those who praise, O Devala—and even toward those who break their compact and deny a good deed done—

sanskrit: uktāś ca na vivakṣanti vaktāram ahite ratam pratihantuṃ na cecchanti hantāraṃ vai manīṣiṇaḥ
english: When spoken against, the wise do not wish to retort upon the speaker bent on their harm, nor do they desire to strike back at one who would strike them.

sanskrit: nāprāptam anuśocanti prāptakālāni kurvate na cātītāni śocanti na cainān pratijānate
english: They do not grieve over what has not come, but do what the present hour demands; they do not mourn things past, nor dwell upon them.

sanskrit: saṃprāptānāṃ ca pūjyānāṃ kāmād artheṣu devala yathopapattiṃ kurvanti śaktimantaḥ kṛtavratāḥ
english: When honored guests arrive, O Devala, in matters of desire and wealth the capable men of fulfilled vows act as circumstance allows.

sanskrit: pakvavidyā mahāprājñā jitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ manasā karmaṇā vācā nāparādhyanti kasya cit
english: Ripe in knowledge, greatly wise, having conquered anger and subdued their senses, they offend against no one in thought, deed, or word.

sanskrit: anīrṣavo na cānyonyaṃ vihiṃsanti kadā cana na ca jātūpatapyante dhīrāḥ parasamṛddhibhiḥ
english: Free from envy, they never do harm to one another, and the steadfast are never tormented by the prosperity of others.

sanskrit: nindāpraśaṃse cātyarthaṃ na vadanti parasya ye na ca nindāpraśaṃsābhyāṃ vikriyante kadā cana
english: They neither utter excessive blame nor excessive praise of another, nor are they ever moved by blame or by praise.

sanskrit: sarvataś ca praśāntā ye sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ na krudhyanti na hṛṣyanti nāparādhyanti kasya cit vimucya hṛdayagranthīṃś caṅkamyante yathāsukham
english: Wholly tranquil, devoted to the welfare of all beings, they neither rage nor exult nor wrong anyone; having loosed the knots of the heart, they wander at their ease.

sanskrit: na yeṣāṃ bāndhavāḥ santi ye cānyeṣāṃ na bāndhavāḥ amitrāś ca na santy eṣāṃ ye cāmitrā na kasya cit
english: They have no kinsmen of their own, nor are they kinsmen to others; they have no enemies, nor are they enemies to anyone.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ kurvate martyāḥ sukhaṃ jīvanti sarvadā dharmam evānuvartante dharmajñā dvijasattama ye hy ato vicyutā mārgāt te hṛṣyanty udvijanti ca
english: Those mortals who live thus dwell ever in happiness, and the knowers of dharma follow dharma alone, O best of the twice-born; but those who fall from this path swing between elation and dismay.

sanskrit: āsthitas tam ahaṃ mārgam asūyiṣyāmi kaṃ katham nindyamānaḥ praśasto vā hṛṣyeyaṃ kena hetunā
english: Standing upon that path, whom should I grudge, and how? Whether blamed or praised, by what cause should I be moved to elation?

sanskrit: yad yad icchanti tan mārgam abhigacchanti mānavāḥ na me nindāpraśaṃsābhyāṃ hrāsavṛddhī bhaviṣyataḥ
english: Men take to whatever path they desire; by blame or by praise I shall suffer neither diminishing nor increase.

sanskrit: amṛtasyeva saṃtṛpyed avamānasya tattvavit viṣasyevodvijen nityaṃ saṃmānasya vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: The knower of truth would take his fill of contempt as though of nectar, and the discerning man would ever shrink from honor as though from poison.

sanskrit: avajñātaḥ sukhaṃ śete iha cāmutra cobhayoḥ vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo yo 'vamantā sa badhyate
english: The despised man sleeps in peace, here and hereafter, in both worlds, freed from all his sins; but the one who despises is himself bound.

sanskrit: parāṃ gatiṃ ca ye ke cit prārthayanti manīṣiṇaḥ etad vrataṃ samāśritya sukham edhanti te janāḥ
english: And whatever wise men seek the supreme goal, those people, taking up this vow, flourish in happiness.

sanskrit: sarvataś ca samāhṛtya kratūn sarvāñ jitendriyaḥ prāpnoti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ yat paraṃ prakṛter dhruvam
english: Drawing in from every quarter all his energies, the man who has mastered his senses attains the abode of Brahman, that which is supreme, beyond Nature, and unchanging.

sanskrit: nāsya devā na gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ padam anvavarohanti prāptasya paramāṃ gatim
english: Once he has reached the supreme goal, neither gods nor Gandharvas, neither Piśācas nor Rākṣasas can trace the path he has trodden.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca priyaḥ sarvasya lokasya sarvasattvābhinanditā guṇaiḥ sarvair upetaś ca ko nv asti bhuvi mānavaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who indeed is the man on earth dear to the whole world, welcomed by all beings, and endowed with every excellence?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi pṛcchato bharatarṣabha ugrasenasya saṃvādaṃ nārade keśavasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this, since you ask, O bull of the Bharatas, I shall recount to you the dialogue of Ugrasena and Keśava concerning Nārada.

sanskrit: ugrasena uvāca paśya saṃkalpate loko nāradasya prakīrtane manye sa guṇasaṃpanno brūhi tan mama pṛcchataḥ
english: Ugrasena said: See how the world warms to the praise of Nārada; I deem him rich in virtues. Tell me this, for I ask you.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca kukurādhipa yān manye śṛṇu tān me vivakṣataḥ nāradasya guṇān sādhūn saṃkṣepeṇa narādhipa
english: Vāsudeva said: O lord of the Kukuras, hear from me, as I would tell them, those noble virtues of Nārada that I count, O ruler of men, set forth in brief.

sanskrit: na cāritranimitto 'syāhaṃkāro dehapātanaḥ abhinnaśrutacāritras tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: In him there is no pride born of good conduct that would bring the body low; his learning and his conduct stand unbroken—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: tapasvī nārado bāḍhaṃ vāci nāsya vyatikramaḥ kāmād vā yadi vā lobhāt tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Nārada is firmly devoted to austerity; in speech he commits no transgression, whether from desire or from greed—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: adhyātmavidhitattvajñaḥ kṣāntaḥ śakto jitendriyaḥ ṛjuś ca satyavādī ca tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Knowing the truth of the science of the inner Self, forbearing, capable, master of his senses, upright and truthful in speech—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: tejasā yaśasā buddhyā nayena vinayena ca janmanā tapasā vṛddhas tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Eminent in splendor, in fame, in intellect, in statecraft and in modesty, in birth and in austerity—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: sukhaśīlaḥ susaṃbhogaḥ subhojyaḥ svādaraḥ śuciḥ suvākyaś cāpy anīrṣyaś ca tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Of pleasant disposition, easy in fellowship, easily fed, gracious in regard, pure, fair of speech and free from envy—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: kalyānaṃ kurute bāḍhaṃ pāpam asmin na vidyate na prīyate parān arthais tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: He works good in full measure; no evil is found in him; he takes no delight in others' wealth—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: vedaśrutibhir ākhyānair arthān abhijigīṣate titikṣur anavajñaś ca tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: By the Vedas, the sacred texts, and the old narratives he seeks to win out in argument; enduring and never contemptuous—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: samatvād dhi priyo nāsti nāpriyaś ca kathaṃ cana manonukūlavādī ca tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Through his evenness none is dear to him nor anyone unwelcome in any way, yet he speaks agreeably to the mind—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: bahuśrutaś caitrakathaḥ paṇḍito 'nalaso 'śaṭhaḥ adīno 'krodhano 'lubdhas tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Deeply learned, a teller of varied tales, wise, never slothful, without guile, never abject, free from anger and from greed—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: nārthe na dharme kāme vā bhūtapūrvo 'sya vigrahaḥ doṣāś cāsya samucchinnās tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Never before has he had a quarrel over wealth, dharma, or pleasure, and his faults are utterly rooted out—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: dṛḍhabhaktir anindyātmā śrutavān anṛśaṃsavān vītasaṃmohadoṣaś ca tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Firm in devotion, blameless in self, learned, full of kindness, and freed from the flaw of delusion—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: asaktaḥ sarvasaṅgeṣu saktātmeva ca lakṣyate adīrghasaṃśayo vāgmī tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Unattached amid all attachments, he yet appears as one whose heart is engaged; quick to resolve his doubts and eloquent—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: samādhir nāsya mānārthe nātmānaṃ stauti karhi cit anīrṣyur dṛḍhasaṃbhāṣas tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: His concentration is never set on winning honor, and he never praises himself; free from envy and steadfast in discourse—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: lokasya vividhaṃ vṛttaṃ prakṛteś cāpy akutsayan saṃsargavidyākuśalas tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Without reviling the world's manifold ways or the natures of men, skilled in the art of company—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: nāsūyaty āgamaṃ kaṃ cit svaṃ tapo nopajīvati avandhyakālo vaśyātmā tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: He grudges no body of learning, and he does not live off his own austerity; his time is never barren, his self is under control—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: kṛtaśramaḥ kṛtaprajño na ca tṛptaḥ samādhitaḥ niyamastho 'pramattaś ca tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: He has done his toil and won his wisdom, yet is never sated in his concentration; fixed in the observances and ever vigilant—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: sāpatrapaś ca yuktaś ca suneyaḥ śreyase paraiḥ abhettā paraguhyānāṃ tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: Possessed of modesty and self-restraint, easily led by others toward the good, and never a betrayer of others' secrets—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: na hṛṣyaty arthalābheṣu nālābheṣu vyathaty api sthirabuddhir asaktātmā tasmāt sarvatra pūjitaḥ
english: He does not exult in the gaining of wealth, nor is he distressed in its loss; steady of mind and unattached in self—therefore he is honored everywhere.

sanskrit: taṃ sarvaguṇasaṃpannaṃ dakṣaṃ śucim akātaram kālajñaṃ ca nayajñaṃ ca kaḥ priyaṃ na kariṣyati
english: Endowed with every virtue, capable, pure, undaunted, knowing the right time and the ways of policy—who would not hold him dear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ādyantaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ śrotum icchāmi kaurava dhyānaṃ karma ca kālaṃ ca tathaivāyur yuge yuge
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I wish to hear, O Kaurava, of the beginning and end of all beings—their contemplation, their action, their measure of time, and likewise their span of life from age to age.

sanskrit: lokatattvaṃ ca kārtsnyena bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim sargaś ca nidhanaṃ caiva kuta etat pravartate
english: And the truth of the worlds in its fullness—the coming and the going of beings, their creation and their dissolution—whence does all this proceed?

sanskrit: yadi te 'nugrahe buddhir asmāsv iha satāṃ vara etad bhavantaṃ pṛcchāmi tad bhavān prabravītu me
english: If your mind is set on showing us favor here, O best of the good, I ask you this; may you declare it to me.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ hi kathitaṃ śrutvā bhṛgubhāṣitam uttamam bharadvājasya viprarṣes tato me buddhir uttamā
english: For having heard before the supreme teaching once spoken by Bhṛgu to the brāhmaṇa-sage Bharadvāja, my understanding thence grew most excellent—

sanskrit: jātā paramadharmiṣṭhā divyasaṃsthānasaṃsthitā tato bhūyas tu pṛcchāmi tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: —it was born wholly devoted to dharma, established upon a heavenly foundation; therefore I ask once more, and you ought to tell it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣye 'ham itihāsaṃ purātanam jagau yad bhagavān vyāsaḥ putrāya paripṛcchate
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall recount to you an ancient tale, that which the lord Vyāsa sang to his son when he inquired.

sanskrit: adhītya vedān akhilān sāṅgopaniṣadas tathā anvicchan naiṣṭhikaṃ karma dharmanaipuṇadarśanāt
english: Having studied all the Vedas entire, with their limbs and Upaniṣads, and seeking the final, conclusive course of action through his insight into the niceties of dharma—

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ vyāsaṃ putro vaiyāsakiḥ śukaḥ papraccha saṃdeham imaṃ chinnadharmārthasaṃśayam
english: —Śuka, son of Vyāsa, asked of his father Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana Vyāsa this doubt, whose perplexity over dharma and meaning was thereby resolved:

sanskrit: bhūtagrāmasya kartāraṃ kālajñāne ca niścayam brāhmaṇasya ca yat kṛtyaṃ tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: "The maker of the host of beings, the certainty in the knowledge of time, and what is the proper task of the brāhmaṇa—that you ought to tell me."

sanskrit: tasmai provāca tat sarvaṃ pitā putrāya pṛcchate atītānāgate vidvān sarvajñaḥ sarvadharmavit
english: To him, his son who asked, the father declared all of this—the learned one who knew the past and the future, the all-knowing, versed in every dharma.

sanskrit: anādyantam ajaṃ divyam ajaraṃ dhruvam avyayam apratarkyam avijñeyaṃ brahmāgre samavartata
english: Without beginning or end, unborn, divine, ageless, unchanging, imperishable, beyond reasoning and beyond knowing—Brahman existed in the beginning.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhā nimeṣā daśa pañca caiva; triṃśat tu kāṣṭhā gaṇayet kalāṃ tām triṃśat kalāś cāpi bhaven muhūrto; bhāgaḥ kalāyā daśamaś ca yaḥ syāt
english: A kāṣṭhā is fifteen blinks of the eye; thirty kāṣṭhās one should reckon a kalā; thirty kalās in turn make a muhūrta—together with that which is a tenth part of a kalā.

sanskrit: triṃśan muhūrtaś ca bhaved ahaś ca; rātriś ca saṃkhyā munibhiḥ praṇītā māsaḥ smṛto rātryahanī ca triṃśat; saṃvatsaro dvādaśamāsa uktaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ dve ayane vadanti; saṃkhyāvido dakṣiṇam uttaraṃ ca
english: Thirty muhūrtas make a day, and a night—such is the reckoning ordained by the sages; thirty days and nights are called a month, and twelve months are declared a year; and those skilled in reckoning say the year has two courses of the sun, the southern and the northern.

sanskrit: ahorātre vibhajate sūryo mānuṣalaukike rātriḥ svapnāya bhūtānāṃ ceṣṭāyai karmaṇām ahaḥ
english: The Sun divides day and night in the world of men: night is for the sleep of beings, and day for the exertion of their works.

sanskrit: pitrye rātryahanī māsaḥ pravibhāgas tayoḥ punaḥ kṛṣṇo 'haḥ karmaceṣṭāyāṃ śuklaḥ svapnāya śarvarī
english: In the realm of the ancestors a month is a day and a night, and again its division is this: the dark fortnight is the day for the exertion of works, the bright fortnight the night for sleep.

sanskrit: daive rātryahanī varṣaṃ pravibhāgas tayoḥ punaḥ ahas tatrodagayanaṃ rātriḥ syād dakṣiṇāyanam
english: In the realm of the gods a year is a day and a night, and again its division is this: there the northward course of the sun is the day, and the southward course is the night.

sanskrit: ye te rātryahanī pūrve kīrtite daivalaukike tayoḥ saṃkhyāya varṣāgraṃ brāhme vakṣyāmy ahaḥkṣape
english: Of that day and night of the gods' world which were first recounted, reckoning their sum of years I shall now declare the day and the night of Brahmā.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃvatsarāgrāṇi pravakṣyāmy anupūrvaśaḥ kṛte tretāyuge caiva dvāpare ca kalau tathā
english: I shall declare in due order the sums of their years in the Kṛta age, the Tretā age, the Dvāpara, and likewise the Kali.
